# Documentation Index

Index for discovering relevant documents during Plan and Explore execution

## Usage

Identify and read task-related sections below:

- Modify `cmd/` or CLI behavior → Read **Specifications** section (CLI, Requirements)
- Modify YAML configuration handling → Read **Specifications** section (Configuration, Requirements)
- Make design decisions or evaluate scope → Read **Project Overview** section
- Edit documents under `docs/` → Read **Contributing** section
- Modify the release workflow, `.goreleaser.yaml`, or `Dockerfile` → Read **Contributing** section (Release Workflow)
- Change explanations for users → Read **User Guide** section and **Contributing** section (Documentation Policy)

## Specifications

- [Requirements](docs/spec/requirements.md): Functional requirements, quality requirements, and invariants of reco - Use when implementing or changing features, or checking supported scope and safety guarantees
- [CLI](docs/spec/cli.md): Commands (`plan`, `apply`, `show`), options, credential selection, interactive approval, output, and exit codes - Use when modifying `cmd/`, adding commands or options, or changing user-visible output and exit codes
- [Configuration](docs/spec/configuration.md): YAML configuration structure, types, allowed values, combinations, management scope interpretation, and input validation - Use when modifying configuration parsing or validation, or adding supported repository settings

## Design

- [Domain Model](docs/design/domain.md): Core concepts of reco and the distinctions between them (declaration, selection, and repository identity; management units vs. managed settings; setting values shared across contexts; side effects; current state vs. observation result and the points in time of observation; reconciliation vs. applicability; change plan structure; logical change vs. update operation; approval and change preconditions; the contexts each concept belongs to) - Use when naming domain types, deciding what a concept means, or checking that code keeps these distinctions
- [Architecture](docs/design/architecture.md): Logical components and their boundaries, change planning and execution control, pre-validation, approval and per-update precondition checks, GitHub API trust boundary (redirects, unmanaged-setting preservation, non-atomic updates), and result classification - Use when placing responsibilities across packages, implementing the plan/apply flow, or changing how GitHub updates are issued and verified

## Research

- [Research](docs/research/README.md): Purpose of the GitHub API research documents, how they are split, and the conventions they follow (grounded only in GitHub official docs, API version basis, developer-verified behavior as notes) - Use when adding a GitHub API fact or a new endpoint document
- [GitHub OpenAPI Excerpt](docs/research/openapi.json): Excerpt of GitHub's official OpenAPI 3.0 description limited to the operations reco uses and the components they reference, generated by `scripts/openapi/update.sh` - Use when checking request or response field types and enum values of an endpoint reco uses
- [GitHub REST API Common](docs/research/rest-api.md): GitHub REST API contract shared by every endpoint reco uses (request URL and headers, API versions, redirects, failure responses, rate limits, conditional requests, token types, scopes, and repository roles) - Use when a spec or design needs a GitHub fact that is not specific to one endpoint
- [GitHub Repositories API](docs/research/repositories.md): Repository get and update endpoints (required permissions, HTTP responses, merge-related field visibility, repository name vs. ID and rename redirects, general setting fields and update behavior) - Use when a spec or design needs a fact about repository identity or general settings
- [GitHub Actions Permissions API](docs/research/actions-permissions.md): Actions permissions, selected actions, and workflow permissions endpoints (required permissions, HTTP responses, fields, update units, and observed side effects) - Use when a spec or design needs a fact about GitHub Actions permission settings

## User Guide

- [User Guide](docs/user-guide/README.md): Entry point of the user guide (intended readers, documents to read for each user goal, and the guide's relationship to the specifications as their source of truth) - Use when choosing which user-facing document to read or adding a new one
- [Glossary](docs/user-guide/glossary.md): Plain-language paraphrases of the terms the user guide uses, grouped by declaration, observation, planning, and applying, with where each term appears in reco's output - Use when writing or reading user-facing explanations, or checking which word the guide uses for a domain concept
- [Configuration Guide](docs/user-guide/configuration.md): How to write the configuration file for users (file location and structure, unwritten settings staying unmanaged, meaning of each setting, what GitHub does when the Actions permission policy changes, listing multiple repositories, common mistakes) - Use when explaining to users how to declare settings, or when changing configuration behavior that users rely on
- [Safety Guide](docs/user-guide/safety.md): What reco guarantees and what it leaves to users, in user-facing terms (not changing undeclared settings, validating every repository before updating, executing only what was approved, stopping when preconditions change or an anomaly occurs, confirming the result before reporting completion, keeping credentials out of output, and what reco does not do such as rollback, retry, or following redirects) - Use when explaining reco's safety behavior to users, or when changing an invariant or behavior that users rely on for trust

## Project Overview

- [Constitution](docs/CONSTITUTION.md): Purpose, problem statement, value proposition, design principles, and non-goals of reco - Use when making design decisions, resolving tradeoffs between principles, or judging whether a feature is in scope

## Contributing

- [Documentation Policy](docs/contributing/docs-policy.md): Responsibilities and sources of truth of each document, identifiers (`FR`, `QR`, `INV`), Relationships (`alignment`, `grounding`, `checks`), consistency checks on change, and the rules for the user guide (position, terms, document dependencies, responsibility boundaries, checks when adding documents, output examples, readers and volume) - Use when adding or changing requirements, identifiers, or Relationship tables, when editing specs and designs, or when editing the user guide
- [Release Workflow](docs/contributing/release.md): Tag-triggered release to GitHub Releases and GHCR (job order and permissions, artifacts, build settings, container image, provenance attestation, partial publication and re-runs, user-side verification, pinning of actions and tools) - Use when modifying `.github/workflows/release.yml`, `.goreleaser.yaml`, or `Dockerfile`, or when cutting a release
